title: CH<SUB>3</SUB>OH and HCN in Interstellar Comet 3I/ATLAS Mapped with the ALMA Atacama Compact Array: Distinct Outgassing Behaviors and a Remarkably High CH<SUB>3</SUB>OH/HCN Production Rate Ratio
question: Measure molecular production rates, kinematics, parent scale lengths, and coma radial temperature profiles of CH3OH and HCN in interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS pre-perihelion, and place it into context with solar system comets.

what.value: Q(OH) = (5.7 +/- 0.6) x 10^28 s^-1 measured at r_H = 1.43 au with the Nancay radio telescope, scaled to derive Q(H2O) for radiative transfer modeling

evidence.quote: In the absence of contemporaneously measured $Q$(H$_2$O) values, we scaled the $Q$(OH)=$(5.7\pm0.6)\times10^{28}$ s$^{-1}$ measured by (cite: Crovisier2025) at *r*~*H*~ = 1.43 au to the *r*~*H*~ of the ACA observations
and OH 18 cm emission with the Nançay radio telescope (cite: Crovisier2025) from October 13–19.
We used explicitly calculated HCN-H$_2$O collisional rates (cite: Zoltowski2025).
Solar photodissociation rates were adopted from (cite: Hrodmarsson2023).

what.value: H2O to OH branching ratio of 85.5%

evidence.quote: assuming insolation-driven (*r*~*H*~$^{-2}$) dependence and an branching ratio of 85.5% (cite: Huebner2015).

what.value: First-pass inner coma rotational temperature T_kin = 60 K (< 5900 km)

evidence.quote: We assumed a gas kinetic temperature $T_{\mathrm{kin}}$ = 60 K as a first pass based on inner coma (nucleocentric distances $<$5900 km) rotational temperatures reported in (cite: Cordiner2025a).

what.value: JCMT HCN (J = 3-2) expansion speed v = 0.46 +/- 0.14 km s^-1 and production rates Q(HCN) = (1.3 +/- 0.4) x 10^25 s^-1 and (4.0 +/- 1.7) x 10^25 s^-1 on September 7 and 14

evidence.quote: our HCN expansion speeds ($\sim$0.2 km s$^{-1}$) are lower than that reported in (cite: Coulson2026) ($v=0.46\pm0.14$ km s$^{-1}$) for September 14
can be compared to their $Q$(HCN) of $(1.3\pm0.4)\times10^{25}$ s$^{-1}$ and $(4.0\pm1.7)\times10^{25}$ s$^{-1}$ on September 7 and 14, respectively.

what.value: Nucleus rotational period of 16.16 hours for 3I/ATLAS

evidence.loc: Complex Line Profile and Production Mechanisms of HCN
evidence.quote: (cite: Santana-Ros2025) found a nucleus rotational period of 16.16 hours for 3I, so our observations on September 12 and 15 (separated by 72 hours) would have sampled very different rotational phases.

what.value: Solar system comet radio mean CH3OH/HCN value of 26 +/- 27 and population means for HCN/H2O and CH3OH/H2O

evidence.quote: with the IR population mean being $\sim0.2$% and the radio mean being $\sim0.1$% (cite: Biver2024).
Our CH$_3$OH/HCN abundance for 3I is $1.2-4.7\sigma$ above the solar system comet mean value of $26\pm27$.

recipe.goal: Calibrate and image ALMA ACA visibility data and transform to cometocentric coordinates
recipe.method: Flag, calibrate, and image in CASA using Högbom deconvolution with natural weighting and a 10'' mask; convolve with synthesized beam, apply Gaussian ACA primary beam correction, and transform to projected cometocentric distances centered on the peak gas flux.
key_parameters: 10'' diameter mask, threshold = 2 x rms noise, natural weighting
ACA primary beam FWHM = 29.3'' at 338 GHz and 27.9'' at 354 GHz
assumptions: Gaussian ACA primary beam response; origin at peak gas flux (<0.75'' offset from phasecenter)

recipe.goal: Construct non-LTE radiative transfer models and sample visibilities in the Fourier domain
recipe.method: Generate 1D and 3D non-LTE radiative transfer model cubes using SUBLIME with Haser radial density profiles, time-average observed visibilities, Fourier-transform model cubes onto the observed uv coverage with vis_sample, and optimize parameters with lmfit.
key_parameters: CH3OH-H2O average collisional cross-section = 5 x 10^-14 cm^-2
Q(OH) = (5.7 +/- 0.6) x 10^28 s^-1 at r_H = 1.43 au; branching ratio = 85.5%
3D cone geometry: phi = phi_STO, psi = psi_sun, gamma = 90 deg
assumptions: Insolation-driven r_H^-2 scaling of Q(H2O) from Q(OH); thermalization approximation for CH3OH-H2O collisions; Haser density distribution; constant expansion velocity in each region

recipe.goal: Retrieve CH3OH kinematics, coma kinetic temperature profiles, parent scale length, and production rates across epochs
recipe.method: First fit parent 1D and 3D models to Sept 18 high-res spectra (with T_kin = 60 K) to get initial kinematics; fix 1D v and Delta v to fit isothermal T_kin = 49 +/- 12 K on Sept 18 low-res J_K = 7_K-6_K lines; adopt T_kin = 49 K to run Delta-chi^2 grid over L_p on Sept 18 high-res spectra; apply 1D models to low-res epochs (scaling v as r_H^-0.5) and retrieve segmented T(r) profiles on Sept 22 and Oct 1.
key_parameters: Initial T_kin = 60 K; retrieved Sept 18 T_kin = 49 +/- 12 K; assumed Aug 28 T_kin = 40 K
Segmented T(r) radial points n = 2 at r = [3500 km, 12,870 km]
Delta-chi^2 thresholds = 1 (1 sigma, 68% confidence) and 6.63 (2.6 sigma, 99% confidence)
assumptions: v scales as r_H^-0.5 on low-resolution dates; parent model (L_p = 0 km) assumed for Aug 28, Sept 22, and Oct 1; constant temperature interior to theta_min/2 and exterior to MRS/2

recipe.goal: Model HCN kinematics, parent scale length, production rates, and test for coma gas acceleration
recipe.method: Fit 1D and 3D SUBLIME models to Sept 12 and 15 high-resolution HCN spectra assuming isothermal T_kin = 45 K, run Delta-chi^2 analysis on L_p, and fit Gaussian profiles to the Sept 15 HCN line as a function of baseline length to measure FWHM vs angular scale.
assumptions: Isothermal coma at T_kin = 45 K; no radial velocity offset allowed in the 3D model

recipe.goal: Fit heliocentric distance power-law to Q(CH3OH) and compute CH3OH/HCN and CH3OH/H2O abundance ratios
recipe.method: Fit a power-law relationship Q(CH3OH)(r_H) to the derived production rates from Aug 28 to Oct 1, interpolate Q(CH3OH) to the Sept 12 and 15 HCN dates to compute CH3OH/HCN ratios, and extrapolate to r_H = 1.43 au to compute CH3OH/H2O.
key_parameters: r_H = 2.17 au (Sept 12), 2.08 au (Sept 15), and 1.43 au (Oct 13-19 OH observations)
assumptions: Power-law dependence of Q(CH3OH) on r_H holds across 2.6 - 1.7 au and extrapolates to 1.43 au

answer_key.quantity: CH3OH/HCN production rate ratio on Sept 12

evidence.quote: the derived CH$_3$OH/HCN ratios in 3I/ATLAS of $124^{+30}_{-34}$ and $79^{+11}_{-14}$ on September 12 and 15, respectively
Using $Q$(HCN) from the best-fit 1D models on these dates, this gives CH$_3$OH/HCN=$124^{+30}_{-34}$ and $79^{+11}_{-14}$.

evidence.quote: Statistical analysis of molecular scale lengths in 3I/ATLAS indicated that CH$_3$OH included production from coma sources at $L_p>258$ km at 99% confidence.
Our $\Delta\chi^2$ curves are shown in Figure [3](#fig:ch3oh-models), and indicate that at 99% confidence there was a source of coma production of CH$_3$OH at $L_p>258$ km.

score_reason: Observing log, calibrators, CASA version, imaging parameters, radiative transfer inputs (rates, cross-sections, H2O scaling formula), and step-by-step Fourier fitting workflow are thoroughly documented, with main numeric results clearly tabulated; slight deductions because SUBLIME is not publicly linked in the paper and visibility time-averaging/grid parameters are omitted.
rediscovery_reason: All three ALMA project codes are explicitly stated, the dataset is compact (8 ACA executions), and the primary scientific claims rest on clear quantitative outputs (production rates, kinematic velocities, scale lengths, and CH3OH/HCN ratios) tabulated in Table 1.
